concept_summary: A 1,540 sq ft restaurant with limited cooking and no alcohol service, converting a retail/vacant space at 3034 24th St in the NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning district within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage and Calle 24 Special Use Districts.

overall.line: Of the 3 approvals this concept needs: 2 further review (zoning and use, building permit and change of use), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with DBI that the 2009 building violations from fire damage (case MB0901179) have been abated, then file a pre-application meeting request with Planning to verify the Calle 24 frontage calculation before committing funds to a CUA application.

lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Restaurant (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-24TH-MISSION: a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 763, in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: Any proposed Restaurant in the sub-area east of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street needs Conditional Use, with or without alcohol. Zoning district NCT-24TH-MISSION lies inside that sub-area: a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(f)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: A new Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar, or the physical expansion of an existing one, is prohibited where those uses take up, or would take up with the project, more than 35% of the commercial frontage (in linear feet) within 300 feet of the site inside the district. The records do not show that share of frontage, so this is not decided (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(1), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Calle 24 Special Use District: Section 249.59 itself does not make a Restaurant, Limited Restaurant or Bar a Conditional Use; its only Conditional Use triggers are storefront mergers over 799 square feet, replacing a Legacy Business and a first-story Health Service. Whether the use needs Conditional Use comes from the underlying district table. This rule asks for nothing here (Planning Code § 249.59(d)(2), in force since before 2022-01-01).
The concept is not described as serving alcohol, so the liquor licence rules of Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District were not applied.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Change of use from restaurant to full restaurant with beer and wine at 2956 24th St (118 m away), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved 2019 after filing in Sept 2018. This is a full use decision (CUA) with detailed conditions.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Approved with extensive standard conditions including hours limited to 6 AM–2 AM, odor control equipment, soundproofing, sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, garbage management, and appointment of a community liaison. These represent the typical condition set for restaurants in this district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Change of use from retail to full-service restaurant (Pig and Pie) at 2962 24th St (107 m away), NCT-24TH-MISSION within the Mission Alcohol SUD, approved 2011. This is a use decision (CUA).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a retail-to-restaurant conversion within the Mission Alcohol SUD on this block with no extracted conditions beyond standard provisions, demonstrating that restaurant use itself is approvable even in the restricted alcohol sub-district when no alcohol service is proposed.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Change of use from office to banquet room (Alma Cocina Restaurant) at 2801 Folsom St (111 m away), NCT-24TH-MISSION, filed Aug 2018 and withdrawn Sept 2018. This is a use decision (CUA) that did not proceed.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This withdrawal shows that not all restaurant CUAs on the corridor succeed; the applicant withdrew within three weeks of filing. The record does not state why, but it demonstrates that operators should verify feasibility before committing significant capital to the project.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for restaurant at 3066 24th St (69 m away, immediately adjacent block), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved Nov 2020 as continuation of existing site use. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referrals for continuation of existing restaurant uses are routinely approved within 30 days. However, this concept is a change of use from retail, so it will require a full CUA hearing, not a quick referral approval.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: DPH referral for restaurant at 2801 Folsom St (111 m), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved Sept 2020 as continuation use under Section 763. This is an agency referral.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Continuation-of-use referrals are approved in 20 days, but they offer no precedent value for a retail-to-restaurant change of use, which requires Conditional Use Authorization and a Commission hearing in NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to allow small self-service restaurant (pastry/espresso/deli, up to 49 seats) at 2980 24th St (77 m), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved April 1990. This is a use decision (CUA).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Small self-service restaurants have been approved on this corridor for over 30 years, establishing a long pattern of support for food-service uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for full-service restaurant at 2980 24th St (77 m, same parcel as 1990.029C), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved April 2001. This is a use decision (CUA).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The same site that received approval for a small restaurant in 1990 received approval to upgrade to full-service restaurant in 2001, showing Planning's willingness to allow evolution of restaurant uses over time on this corridor.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for full-service restaurant on ground floor at 2801 Folsom St (111 m), NCT-24TH-MISSION, approved Aug 1994. This is a use decision (CUA).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Full-service restaurants have been approved at nearby Folsom and 24th St locations since at least 1994, demonstrating three decades of precedent for restaurant uses in this immediate area of the NCT-24TH-MISSION district.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm in writing with SF Department of Building Inspection Code Enforcement that the 2009 building violations from fire damage (case MB0901179) have been abated.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Search the address 3034 24th St in DBI's online records system or call Code Enforcement at 415-575-6863 to ask whether any notices of violation remain open from the 2009 fire damage case. If violations are still open, they must be corrected before a health permit or CUA can be issued, per the 2009 Planning decision. Obtain a letter or screen capture showing no open violations, and attach it to the CUA application.

filing_playbook.action: Appear at the Planning Commission hearing (or authorize your representative to appear) to present the project and answer Commissioner questions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At the hearing, emphasize that the project is a change of use from vacant retail to an active, neighborhood-serving restaurant with no alcohol, limited cooking, and standard hours. timeline_cost.notes: The day and cost ranges cover the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Commission), health permit to operate (DPH), and building permit with change of use (DBI). The CUA is the long pole: 120–300 days from filing to Commission approval, per the catalog entry for a conditional use authorization in San Francisco, and comparable restaurant CUAs in this district took 20–408 days to approval (N = 8 approved cases). Government costs include the CUA filing fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost, with potential First Year Free fee waiver for new storefront businesses), the health plan check fee ($828–$2,207), the health permit application fee ($470), and the building permit fee ($800–$15,000 as a percentage of construction valuation). These are times and costs to obtain the approvals when they are granted; they do not account for the scenario where the Calle 24 frontage cap prohibits the project or where the applicant withdraws. The timeline assumes no appeals and that the DBI violations from the 2009 fire damage have been abated before filing begins. Add 60–120 days if the CUA is appealed to the Board of Supervisors. The building permit review (14–120 days) and health permit issuance (14–45 days) run after the CUA is approved, so the total time from first filing to opening is roughly 150–465 days, not including pre-application research or construction time.

records_summary: 3034 24th St lies in the NCT-24TH-MISSION zoning district where a Restaurant is a conditional use. The property sits inside both the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (which requires Conditional Use for any proposed restaurant in this sub-area) and the Calle 24 Special Use District (which prohibits new restaurants where they would exceed 35% of commercial frontage within 300 ft, though the records do not show the current share). The site has one prior planning record: a 2009 referral for a restaurant use that was denied because building violations from fire damage had not been abated. The immediate block is saturated with food and drink businesses: 14 registered establishments within 500 ft (N=14), 3 bars, and 6 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, triggering an undue-concentration flag. Within 1,000 ft in this zoning district over the last 10 years there were only 5 dated use decisions for comparable businesses (1 approved, 2 approved with conditions, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn)—too few for a rate.
